messages:
alice: Quick check-in on the SDK surface follow-up from the RFC — focusing on transport + retry + pagination tradeoffs.
ben: TL;DR: want a single ergonomic object for retries that works across Python/TS/Go without forcing language-specific shims.
chandra: Agree. Also need clarity on who owns resume tokens vs server session. We keep seeing incompat bugs when a transport adds a session header implicitly.
dmitri: Proposal: transport carries an opaque session id only for connection affinity; pagination/resume tokens are application-level and round-tripped in the payload.
eva: That seems safer. If transports mutate resume tokens (eg compress/encode) we get untenable coupling. :eyes:
alice: For retries, we debated "policy as data" vs builder helpers. Ben suggested a RetryPolicy struct with fields: max_attempts, backoff_ms, idempotency_predicate.
ben: Example in pseudocode:
```
RetryPolicy(policy_name="default", max_attempts=4, backoff="exponential(100, 2)", idempotent_paths=["GET", "LIST"]) 
client.call(..., retry=RetryPolicy)
```
chandra: Language ergonomics matter: Python wants keyword args, TS wants an interface, Go wants a concrete type. But semantics must match.
dmitri: Implementation note: transports should accept a retry callback hook so they can apply transport-level quick-fail (circuit-breaker) before performing SDK-level retry logic.
eva: How do we handle streaming/paged endpoints? If a stream errors mid-way, do we auto-resume with a token or bubble to app?
alice: Tradeoff: auto-resume hides partial progress but improves UX for idempotent stream consumers. We should default to bubble-to-app and provide an opt-in resume policy.
ben: Suggestion: two-layer API: paged iterator yields objects and exposes `resume_token()`; SDK's high-level helpers can call `auto_resume(policy)` which uses the token + RetryPolicy.
chandra: That matches our safety posture. Also add telemetry hooks: retry_count, resumed, resume_token_used.
dmitri: Edge case: prefetch + backpressure. If client prefetches N pages then server-side resume token semantics must be stable. We should document model expectations clearly.
eva: Also mention cross-language tests: add a tiny harness that runs Python/TS/Go against a mock transport that simulates transient errors + token changes.
alice: Action items: (1) draft RetryPolicy shape and examples in three lang styles, (2) spec transport session vs application resume boundary, (3) implement auto_resume helper behind opt-in flag, (4) add cross-lang integration test. I'll open a follow-up PR with the shapes. :rocket:
ben: Sounds good. I'll prototype the TS interface and add an example to the SDK README.
chandra: I'll write the docs section about invariants (resume tokens immutable, transports must be transparent) and the telemetry fields.
dmitri: I'll sketch the transport hook API and a minimal mock server for tests.
eva: If anyone wants pair-review on the TS prototype ping me. :+1:
alice: OK closing this thread — we can move specifics to the PRs. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
